metadata.title: Transformación digital de la administración tributaria ecuatoriana y reducción de la evasión fiscal mediante facturación electrónica, inteligencia artificial y control preventivo.
metadata.description: La digitalización de la administración tributaria ecuatoriana ha ampliado la capacidad institucional para registrar operaciones, contrastar declaraciones y orientar controles preventivos, se planteó como objetivo analizar la contribución de la facturación electrónica, la inteligencia artificial y los mecanismos automatizados al cumplimiento tributario y a la reducción de espacios asociados con evasión fiscal. Se aplicó un enfoque mixto de predominio cualitativo, con diseño documental, descriptivo, analítico, no experimental y longitudinal retrospectivo, se revisaron normas, literatura especializada y estadísticas oficiales del Servicio de Rentas Internas correspondientes a 2019-2025, se identificó un aumento de 47,2 por ciento en la recaudación comparable y cumplimiento superior al cien por ciento en cinco de siete años. Se concluyó que la transformación digital fortalece trazabilidad, disponibilidad de información y detección de inconsistencias, aunque la evidencia no permite atribuir causalidad exclusiva sobre la evasión, debido a la influencia del ciclo económico, reformas normativas, informalidad, cultura tributaria y brechas de acceso tecnológico.

metadata.title: Acoustic field prediction during the launch of rockets
metadata.description: This work presents the prediction of noise generated during the launch of space rockets. A semiempirical model was applied, using as input data the physical and geometric characteristics of the jet of gases propelled by the rocket, which acts as the primary source of noise. The model is based on the one originally proposed by Eldred back in 1971 and its subsequent modifications. We expanded the model with expressions for the estimation of the acoustic power of noise sources. To validate the prediction in a particular case, we have considered the launch of the VEGA rocket from European Space Agency, at the launchpad located in Kourou (French Guiana). Using as reference experimental data recorded during a launch, the study confirms that the semi-empirical model predicts the acoustic field generated during the launch with great precision, especially in the low and medium frequencies, which are the most interesting from the point of view of impact that this noise has on the rocket and its load.

metadata.title: llm-ensemble-effective-diversity: analysis code and data
metadata.description: Analysis code and data for a study of the semantic dispersion of a sixteen-model language model ensemble on psychotherapeutic case formulation, a task for which no correctness criterion is available. The effective number of voices is the Vendi Score, computed with the reference implementation rather than reimplemented; the per-voice dissent contribution is original to the study, and decomposes the ensemble's mean pairwise dissent rather than the spectral index. Includes the per-run indices, the per-model dissent contributions and the formulations produced by the panel: 7,200 model-run cells planned, 7,160 formulations obtained, and 7,082 analysed after the validity filter. The released JSONL carries all 7,200 records, each with the status that places it in one of the three counts. Dual-licensed: Apache License 2.0 for the analysis code (src/, figures/) and Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 for the published data and documentation (data/, docs/); see LICENSE and LICENSE-DATA in the repository. The vignette bank is not included and is held in a separate restricted deposit, doi 10.5281/zenodo.21708455. Effect sizes for the fixed-effects analyses are classical eta squared, the sum of squares of the effect over the total sum of squares of the response; v1.0.2 is the first version to compute them that way and earlier versions differ in that denominator alone, not in any underlying analysis. metadata.title: ACCESIBILIDAD Y CALIDAD EN LA ORGANIZACIÓN DE EVENTOS: PROPUESTA DE UN MODELO DE EVENT PLANNER PARA TODAS LAS EDADES EN LA CIUDAD DE TARMA, PERÚ
metadata.description:
Resumen

La organización de eventos ha dejado de ser solo una reunión familiar para convertirse en una industria de experiencias. En ciudades como Tarma, donde la tradición festiva es muy fuerte, existe una alta demanda de servicios de planificación; sin embargo, el mercado local suele ofrecer opciones muy costosas o demasiado fragmentadas. El objetivo de esta investigación fue diseñar un modelo de negocio de Event Planner que ofrezca paquetes accesibles y de calidad para todos los segmentos de edad. Se utilizó una metodología cuantitativa de nivel descriptivo, aplicando una encuesta a 120 residentes de Tarma. Los resultados mostraron que el 68% de los consumidores prioriza la accesibilidad económica sin sacrificar la personalización, y existe una alta aceptación por los servicios integrales. Se concluye que un modelo de negocio basado en la segmentación por edades y la flexibilidad de precios resulta altamente viable y responde a una necesidad real del mercado tarmeño.

metadata.title: Cumplimiento de los protocolos de bioseguridad por parte del personal de enfermería en hospitales públicos
metadata.description: La bioseguridad constituye uno de los pilares de la atención sanitaria segura, ya que orienta las prácticas destinadas a reducir la exposición a riesgos biológicos tanto para los pacientes como para el personal de salud. A pesar de la existencia de protocolos ampliamente difundidos y de programas institucionales orientados a fortalecer la prevención y el control de infecciones, diversos estudios evidencian que el grado de cumplimiento continúa siendo heterogéneo entre instituciones, servicios hospitalarios y profesionales, situación que incrementa la probabilidad de infecciones asociadas a la atención sanitaria y accidentes laborales. En los hospitales públicos, donde convergen una elevada demanda asistencial, limitaciones de recursos y una compleja dinámica organizacional, comprender los factores relacionados con la adherencia a las medidas de bioseguridad representa una necesidad para fortalecer la seguridad del paciente y la protección del talento humano. El presente estudio tuvo como objetivo analizar el cumplimiento de los protocolos de bioseguridad por parte del personal de enfermería que labora en hospitales públicos, identificando los factores asociados que influyen en su adherencia. Se desarrolló una investigación con enfoque cuantitativo, de diseño no experimental, corte transversal y alcance descriptivo-correlacional. Los datos fueron analizados mediante estadística descriptiva e inferencial para establecer la relación entre las variables de estudio. Se espera que los resultados permitan identificar fortalezas y debilidades en la aplicación de los protocolos de bioseguridad, así como reconocer la influencia de factores individuales e institucionales sobre el nivel de cumplimiento.

metadata.title: Hygrocybe jarabacoensis Angelini, Dovana, Lodge, M. Marchetti & Vizzini 2026, sp. nov.
metadata.description:
Hygrocybe jarabacoensis Angelini, Dovana, Lodge, M. Marchetti & Vizzini sp. nov.

Figs 5, 6

Etymology.

The specific epithet jarabacoensis refers to the type locality, Jarabacoa, a town in the Central Mountain Range of the Dominican Republic where the species was collected.

Diagnosis.

Differing from H. chloochlora in the absence of a membranous marginal fringe and a perforation on the pileus and divergence in ribosomal sequences.

Types.

Dominican Republic, La Vega, Jarabacoa 19.188667, –70.592655, 7 March 2020, C. Angelini, JBSD 141872 Holotype (ANGE 1374 Isotype). GenBank: ITS = PZ 148590, LSU = PZ 145851.

Description.

Pileus 25–40 mm diam., convex then plane, sometimes becoming depressed but not perforated at center, margin not lobed and not striate; surface dry or moist but not viscid, radially fibrillose-rugose and cracked in age, strongly rimose if dry, yellow-green, reddish (brownish) - green. Lamellae adnate-emarginate or decurrent with a tooth, ventricose, up to 7 mm broad, intercalated with 1–2 lengths of lamellulae, olive green, yellow-green, thick, and distant, with pale, irregular eroded edge. Stipe 45–75 × 2–5 mm, elongate, straight and ± cylindrical, greenish white towards the apex, tinted pale red or yellow towards the base, white at base; surface smooth, pruinose, covered with small white flakes, solid or slightly fistulose. Context up to 1–2 mm thick, greenish white in the pileus, reddish white in the stipe, immutable. Odor and taste indistinct.

Basidiospores strongly dimorphic: macrospores (13.5 –) 15.7– 17.5 – 19.4 (– 21.0) × (8.0 –) 9.1– 10.1 – 11.0 (– 12.0) µm, [95 / 6 / 3], Q = 1.60– 1.75 – 1.90, V = 689– 948 – 1206 µm 3, oblong, rarely ellipsoid, sometimes with a subplane adaxial side, inamyloid, thin- to slightly thick-walled (wall up to 1 µm), hyaline, mostly with refractive guttulate content, occasionally with a large inner guttula, without a suprahilar depression, with mostly obtuse apex, and distinct hilar appendix; microspores (5.0 –) 5.9– 6.5 – 7.2 (– 8.0) × (3.0 –) 3.5– 3.96 – 4.4 (– 5.0) µm [120 / 6 / 3], Q = 1.50– 1.65 – 1.81, V = 39.0– 54.9 – 70.9 µm 3, ellipsoid to oblong, inamyloid, thin- to slightly thick-walled [wall up to 0.5 (– 0.8) µm thick], hyaline, with one or more guttules and with evident hilar appendix. Basidia clearly dimorphic: macrobasidia (30.0 –) 37.0– 43.8 – 50.6 (– 57.5) × (12.0 –) 14.1– 16.3 – 18.4 (– 21.0) µm [41 / 6 / 3], clavate, ventricose, often with more or less long peduncle, with large medallion clamp at base, tetrasporic to bisporic, sterigmata up to 8 μm long, thin- to thick-walled (wall up to 1 µm thick), hyaline, guttulate; microbasidia (17.0 –) 20.8– 24.4 – 28.0 (– 31.5) × (5.0 –) 6.0–6.8 – 7.6 (– 8.5) μm [77 / 6 / 3], Q = 3.0– 3.6 – 4.3, V = 428– 607 – 786 µm 3, narrowly clavate to clavate, mostly with more or less long peduncle, with medallion clamp at base, tetrasporic to bisporic, sterigmata up to 9 (– 10) μm long, thin-walled to slightly thick-walled (wall up to 0.5 µm thick) apically, hyaline and often internally guttulate. Pleurocystidia absent. Lamellar edge shows pseudocystidia (sterile elements that originate from the hymenophoral trama hyphae) and cheilocystidia. Pseudocystidia 30–120 × 8–15 μm, subcylindrical, lageniform, subfusiform, sometimes reclined, straight or sinuous, sometimes septate, thin-walled, hyaline, often with refractive guttulate deposits, with rounded to subacute apex. Cheilocystidia abundant, mostly localized near the stipe, broadly clavate to subcylindrical, 20–40 × 8–15 µm, with a more or less long peduncle, hyaline, without inner guttulae. Hymenophoral trama regular to subregular; a mixture of short, clavate, swollen, fusiform, 20–50 µm wide hyphae and long subcylindrical, often> 500 µm × 5–20 (– 30) μm hyphae, often tapered towards the septa; thin- to thick-walled (to 1.5 µm thick), faintly yellowish colored, with a hyaline to pale yellowish cytoplasmic pigment; rare thromboplerous hyphae, 2–5 µm wide, sinuous and with yellowish contents. Pileipellis as a subregular cutis, consisting of a) mostly fusiform parallel (repent) hyphae, over 200 µm long, 10–20 µm wide, some with an adscending terminal element, with yellowish-ochre cytoplasmic contents; b) thin hyphae with an irregular pattern, intertwined, exceeding 200 µm long, 3–5 µm wide, thin-walled, hyaline or slightly greenish under optical microscopy. Discontinuously, there are also tufts of emerging pileocystidioid hyphae with a morphology similar to that of pseudocystidia (see picture ANGE 1940). Occasional thromboplerous hyphae with yellowish contents. Subcutis subregular to irregular, made up of short fusiform, subvesicular elements, and fusiform hyphae even over 200 µm long and 20–40 (– 50) μm wide, thin-walled. Stipitipellis a cutis composed of parallel cylindrical hyphae, 3–10 μm wide, thin to slightly thick-walled (to 1.0 µm thick), with a yellowish cytoplasmic pigment, producing, especially at the stipe apex, copious and characteristic tufts of caulocystidia 20–60 × 6–20 µm which have a morphology similar to those present on the lamellar edge near the stipe. There are also thin hyphae with an irregular pattern, intertwined, exceeding 200 µm long, 3–5 µm wide, thin-walled, hyaline or slightly greenish, similar to those found in the pileipellis. Stipititrama regular, consisting of parallel hyphae even over 200 µm long, 5–15 (– 20) μm wide, thin-walled, mostly hyaline. Clamp-connections present throughout.

Habit, habitat, occurrence, and distribution.

Growing solitary on litter in mountain forests with conifers (Pinus occidentalis Sw.). Quite common.

Additional specimens examined.

Dominican Republic, La Vega, Jarabacoa 19.188667, –70.592655, 7 December 2016, C. Angelini (ANGE 888); ibidem, 12 December 2023 (ANGE 1940).

Notes.

This species is characterized by its medium-sized basidiomata, a radially fibrillose pileus, a long stipe, yellowish-reddish-green tinges on the pileus, lamellae, and stipe, and the presence of macro- and microbasidiospores. The three nrITS sequences of H. jarabacoensis clustered in a highly supported clade (SH-aLRT = 84, UFB = 100, BPP = 0.98). In the phylogeny, the / H. jarabacoensis clade is sister to the sequence of H. chloochlora from Puerto Rico (SAC-PR- 9899, GenBank KF 381522). The nrITS sequence from the holotype of H. jarabacoensis revealed 95 % sequence identity (578 of 609 base pairs) and a gap occurrence of 3 % (19 of 609 base pairs) when compared with the nrITS sequence of H. chloochlora from Puerto Rico (GenBank KF 381522). Both are placed within a more inclusive supported clade (SH-aLRT = 92, UFB = 98, BPP = 0.99) that includes H. appalachianensis (TENN: 61606) and four sequences from Belize deposited in GenBank as H. aff. chloochlora (CFMR BZ-3042, EU 435147, Hygrocybe smaragdus Lodge, T. J. Baroni & Aime, nom. prov., ined.), H. aff. prieta (CFMR BZ-3099, GenBank KF 291168, Hygrocybe elongatipes Lodge, T. J. Baroni & Aime, nom. prov., ined.; BRH; CFMR), and H. aff. neofirma (CFMR BZ-1926, KF 291166; BRH; PUL).

Among the species of Hygrocybe with green coloration, H. jarabacoensis differs from H. chloochlora Pegler & Fiard from the Caribbean and H. aff. chloochlora from Belize in lacking a membranous marginal fringe on the pileus; it also lacks a perforated pileus, whereas H. chloochlora usually has a pileus perforated at the center (Pegler and Fiard 1978; Pegler 1983; Lodge and Pegler 1990; Lodge, pers. obs.). In addition, the macrospores of H. jarabacoensis (14–21 × 8–11 µm) are larger than those of H. aff. chloochlora from Belize (10.7–15.2 × 6.4–8.4 µm). Among Hygrocybe species in section Pseudofirmae from the Caribbean Basin with purple or dusky tints on the pileus, H. jarabacoensis shares the presence of waxy, furfuraceous scales on the stipe with H. prieta Lodge & Pegler but differs in lacking a perforated pileus with a sterile fringe and in having larger macrospores (14–21 × 8–11 vs. 10–17 × 7–9 µm) (Lodge and Pegler 1990).

metadata.title: Instances for the Flexible Multi-Period Multi-Depot Capacitated Vehicle Routing Problem with Time Windows
metadata.description: The FMPMD-CVRP-TW instances are adapted from the classical periodic vehicle-routing (PVRP) benchmark data, and are stated here for a Flexible Multi-Period Multi-Depot Capacitated Vehicle Routing Problem with Time Windows. Each instance describes a network of two depots and n customers served over a planning horizon of T days. Depot 1 coincides with node 0 of the customer graph, so the first row of the depot-to-node distance matrix reproduces row 0 of the node-to-node matrix; depot 2 is a distinct location, present only through its own row of distances, and its distance to depot 1 is fixed at 50 in every instance. Demand is flexible rather than fixed: each customer carries a nominal demand W_i and may be served any quantity inside the interval [wmin_i, wmax_i], set throughout at [0.25 W_i, 0.75 W_i]. The visit interval duedate_i inherited from the source PVRP data (2, 4, 6 or 12 days) is retained in the files but is not binding under the single-visit model; it is what generates the spread of nominal demands, since a customer visited less often accumulates more between visits.

data.title: Instances for the Flexible Multi-Period Multi-Depot Capacitated Vehicle Routing Problem with Time Windows

metadata.title: Instances for the Two-Echelon Capacitated Vehicle Routing Problem with Intermediate Facilities
metadata.description: The 2E-CVRP-IF instances are derived from real operational data of Saltillo, Coahuila (Mexico)'s municipal solid waste morning-shift collection system. The network comprises four node types: a depot (D) from which collection vehicles (CVs) depart and return; customer nodes representing urban settlements whose demand and service time are derived from residential population; two intermediate facilities (IF1, IF2) where CVs unload and synchronize with transportation vehicles (TVs); and a landfill (L) from which TVs operate. Customer demand is estimated at 1.8 kg per inhabitant per day, allocating one-third of weekly generation to the morning shift, and service time is proportional to population. Any customer whose demand exceeds the maximum CV capacity of 12,000 kg is replaced by an equivalent number of identical sub-nodes, so the actual node count stored in a file may exceed the nominal count appearing in its filename.

data.title: Instances for the Two-Echelon Capacitated Vehicle Routing Problem with Intermediate Facilities

metadata.title: A Complex Case of Recurrent Pulmonary Tuberculosis, Pulmonary Aspergillosis and Systemic Multiorgan Failure
metadata.description:
Abstract

Recurrent pulmonary tuberculosis is rare in low-incidence settings and is most frequently associated with relapse, reinfection, drug resistance or immunocompromise (Vega et al., 2021; Vega et al., 2024). Chronic pulmonary aspergillosis is a recognised complication of previous cavitary tuberculosis and may present with overlapping clinical and radiological features, making diagnosis challenging (Denning et al., 2011).

This case report describes a 52-year-old male with a third presentation of pulmonary tuberculosis and established chronic pulmonary aspergillosis. This patient’s admission was complicated by acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS), septic shock, acute kidney injury requiring renal replacement therapy and prolonged invasive mechanical ventilation requiring tracheostomy. Despite an initially poor prognosis, he gradually recovered following anti-tuberculous therapy, antifungal treatment, intensive organ support and multidisciplinary rehabilitation.

journal.title: Journal of MAR Pulmonology and Respiratory Medicine

metadata.title: Extensión de las cláusulas arbitrales a partes no signatarias en Venezuela
metadata.description: El presente artículo tuvo como finalidad analizar la extensión de las cláusulas arbitrales hacia las partes no signatarias en el ordenamiento jurídico venezolano. La investigación aplicó un enfoque cualitativo y un diseño documental. Se utilizó la técnica del fichaje para registrar unidades de análisis, con ocho (8) sentencias del Tribunal Supremo de Justicia y tribunales de instancia por su relevancia en arbitraje y materia contractual. Para establecer el significado de las variables se empleó la interpretación extensiva. Se obtuvo como resultado que la escrituralidad de la cláusula arbitral es un requisito probatorio y la ausencia de la firma de los involucrados no es obstáculo para determinar quién es parte arbitral o no. Por último, la teoría de los actos propios es aplicable en el arbitraje venezolano conforme al principio de buena fe. Se concluyó que en Venezuela es viable, excepcionalmente, la extensión de la cláusula a sujetos que no la suscribieron formalmente, si cumplen los supuestos excepcionales de la teoría de los actos propios en el arbitraje, para garantizar seguridad jurídica.
